name: Koto
tagline: Brand agency with five offices, showing identity work for Instagram, Amazon and Microsoft
description:
Koto is a creative agency with offices in Los Angeles, New York, London, Berlin and Sydney. The homepage calls it "The Creative Company" and says the five offices work as one studio.

The homepage shows five projects with a short text for each: the Instagram wordmark, the Amazon brand system, Microsoft Copilot+PC, Fitbit Ace LTE and Tripadvisor. The Amazon text says the project ran 18 months across 15 markets and more than 50 sub-brands. A news item says Koto bought Stereo Creative, a studio of 60 people.

The site is a Next.js build. It has a showreel, a services page, a careers section and a sitemap with 54 project URLs. It shows no prices.
pricing_detail: No published rates. The homepage gives press and office email addresses and a careers link, but no price or plan.
agent_guidance:
Use Koto as a benchmark for a large brand agency that sells identity systems to global tech and consumer brands. Read the five homepage project texts for scope language: markets, sub-brands, duration.

The sitemap lists 54 project pages, so go there for more cases. Do not expect prices or a process page with numbers. The homepage is image-heavy and the text sits between the project images.
why_it_matters: It shows how a large brand agency presents global identity work with short, factual project texts next to the images.
tier_reason: Five named projects for Instagram, Amazon, Microsoft, Google and Tripadvisor, with scope figures, and 54 project URLs in the sitemap. Held below S because only the homepage was read, the site has no llms.txt, and it gives no prices.

name: 1/1 Studio
tagline: Identity studio led by Natasha Mead, with every project and deliverable numbered on one index page
description:
1/1 Studio (also written 1 of 1 Studio) is a design studio for brand identity and creative direction. The about page says Natasha Mead founded and leads it, and that the team is deliberately small.

The homepage is one index of 17 projects. Each project has a number, a year range, a list of deliverables and up to a dozen numbered images, for example "01.2.3 Business Cards". Clients include Field Studies Flora, Simone Bodmer–Turner, Ne Geurra, Yu Mei and F.Miller. The work covers identity, print, packaging, websites and e-commerce builds.

The site is a Next.js build. The footer shows a clock in NZT and a newsletter called the 1/1 Dispatch. It shows no prices.
pricing_detail: No published rates. Enquiries go to office@1of1studio.com.
agent_guidance:
Use this as a reference for an index-style portfolio, where the numbering system is the layout. Each project lists its deliverables (Brand Identity, Print Assets, Website Development) above its images, so you can read the scope of each job from the page text.

The about page explains the studio. The work pages carry the detail. Do not look for prices or a services page with numbers.
why_it_matters: It shows a studio portfolio that uses a numbering system instead of a hero, with the deliverables of each project in plain text.
tier_reason: 17 projects with numbered deliverables and named clients, and an about page that names the founder. Held below A because it gives no prices, no llms.txt, and the sitemap lists one URL only.
notable_for: founded and led by Natasha Mead

name: Percept Brand Design Agency
tagline: Sydney branding and packaging agency with a type-led homepage and long SEO copy
description:
Percept is a branding, design and creative agency in Sydney, Australia. The site groups its work under Branding, Packaging, Communication and Digital.

The homepage names four client projects: Endeavour Mutual and Mondiale VGL (rebrands), Mizzica (branding and packaging) and Insure&Go (corporate identity). The rest of the page is long text about the agency, written for search, and two client quotes. A form and a "Request a Quote" link start a project.

The site runs on WordPress. It shows no prices.
pricing_detail: No published rates. The site asks you to request a quote through a form or by email to info@percept.com.au.
agent_guidance:
Use the first screen only as a reference: a type-led opener where the phrase after "We’re in the business of" rotates. The lower homepage is long SEO copy that repeats "creative agency Sydney", so do not copy its structure.

The work is grouped under Branding, Packaging, Communication and Digital in the menu. Expect no prices.
why_it_matters: It is an example of a regional brand agency site that pairs a strong type-led opener with search-driven body copy.
tier_reason: Four named client projects and two client quotes are on the homepage. Held at C because most of the page is SEO text, the work is shown only as thumbnails, and the site has no prices and no llms.txt.
notable_for: long SEO copy below the fold

name: Poch Studio
tagline: Brand and web studio with four fixed-price packages from $1500 on the homepage
description:
Poch Studio is a design studio for brand identity, web design, packaging, illustration and 3D. The meta description calls it a studio of friends who help brands "bloom".

The homepage shows five case studies with a short text each: Avant-Garde Territory (an identity for Ural constructivist architecture), Open Office, Trapeze (a Jerusalem disco party), Crystal Car (VFX commercials) and Modern Mayr Dilijan (a no-code site built in Readymag).

The homepage also lists four packages with prices: Sprint at $1500, Start-Up at $3000, The Identity at $3000 and Bombastic at $6000+. An FAQ and a free intro call follow. The site is a Framer build.
pricing_detail: Four fixed packages on the homepage: Sprint $1500 (base identity, one revision), Start-Up $3000 (base identity, landing page, no-code build), The Identity $3000 (full brand identity and guidelines), and Bombastic $6000+ (full identity, brandbook, multipage site, custom development, social, motion and 3D). Extras are priced individually. The intro call is free.
agent_guidance:
Use Poch as a reference for a small studio that publishes package prices next to its case studies. The package cards show how to list scope per tier in plain words.

The case study texts are in the HTML and name the client, the problem and the output. The 3D work and the motion live in images and video, so read them in a browser.
why_it_matters: Few branding studios publish prices. This one lists four packages with dollar figures and the scope of each.
tier_reason: Five case studies with clear texts and four priced packages on the homepage. Held below A because the cases are small regional projects, and the site has no llms.txt and a one-URL sitemap.
evidence: Fetched https://poch.studio/ with curl on 2026-11-24: 200, no redirect, about 531 KB, Framer markers (data-framer, framerusercontent). Title "Poch Studio". The page reads "Logos are just the tip of the iceberg.", "Clear structure, strong visuals, no fluff.", and "website for Armenia’s first Modern Mayr Medicine center, built entirely without code". Package prices $1500, $3000, $3000 and $6000+ are in the HTML. https://poch.studio/sitemap.xml 200 with one URL. https://poch.studio/llms.txt 404.

name: Resonance Studio
tagline: AI-focused brand and product studio for startups, sold as Brand and Product Sprints
description:
The Resonance Studio calls itself "the human creative studio for the AI era". It works with startups and sells its work as two sprints: a Brand Sprint (strategy, identity, web design and build) and a Product Sprint (prototype, validation, web and iOS app). It also runs a venture track and an AI upskill program.

The homepage shows three projects, all Brand Sprints: Zeroshot Data, Endless Commerce and Equilibrium Energy. Five founder testimonials follow. One says the team went "from idea to product in market doing over 40k in MRR in 90 days".

The site is a Webflow build. It has a Supply shop for tools and templates. The homepage shows no prices, and the footer reads 2024.
pricing_detail: No prices on the homepage. Work is sold as Brand Sprints and Product Sprints, booked through the site.
agent_guidance:
Use this as a reference for a studio that sells fixed sprints instead of open projects, and that leads with AI in its offer. The sprint cards list scope in short lines.

The llms.txt exists but holds Webflow page dumps, including a style guide with lorem ipsum and the privacy policy. Do not treat it as a curated summary. Only three projects are on the homepage.
why_it_matters: It shows how a studio packages brand and product work as sprints for AI startups.
tier_reason: Clear sprint offer and five named testimonials. Held at C because only three projects are shown, the homepage gives no prices, and the llms.txt is an unedited page dump.
notable_for: Brand Sprint and Product Sprint offers

name: Analogue Agency
tagline: Amsterdam brand and Framer website agency, with fixed-fee project types on a pricing page
description:
Analogue is a brand and digital design agency in Amsterdam. The meta description says it builds identity systems and Framer websites for product brands like Vitra, Polaroid and Tony's Chocolonely. The homepage says its Vitra case won Framer Website of the Year.

The homepage is mostly motion and a few links: work, team, contact and a book club. The sitemap lists 32 case pages, among them Vitra, Tony's Chocolonely, Atomic, Equip and Ask Phill.

The pricing page says Analogue prices by the project, with a fixed fee, team and timeline. It lists five project types, from Identity + Landing to Flagship E-commerce. The price figures do not show in the static HTML. The site is a Framer build.
pricing_detail: Fixed fee per project, divided into sprints. The pricing page lists Identity + Landing, Identity + Site, No Code E-commerce, Flagship E-commerce and Campaign Website, with one example at 6 weeks. The fee figures load in the browser and are not in the static HTML.
agent_guidance:
Use Analogue as a reference for a brand agency that also builds in Framer, and for a pricing page that sells fixed project types. Open /about-us/pricing in a browser to see the figures.

The homepage text is split into single letters for animation, so scraped text is hard to read. Use the sitemap to find the 32 case pages.
why_it_matters: It is a brand agency that publishes its pricing model and project types, and its Vitra site won a Framer award.
tier_reason: 32 case pages, named clients such as Vitra and Leica, and a pricing page with fixed project types. Held below A because the homepage holds little text, the fee figures are not in the HTML, and there is no llms.txt.
notable_for: Vitra case won Framer Website of the Year

name: That Thing
tagline: London brand studio for positioning, identity and copy, with twelve projects on the homepage
description:
That Thing is a brand studio at 170 Bermondsey St, London. The homepage says it builds brands "that make business change happen".

The homepage shows twelve selected projects, each with a one-line summary: Abbey Road, Fitr, Lone Wolves Club, Easyfundraising, Happy Fruit, Gravis, Designyatra, Weed.de, Leva and Celsius Industries among them. A filter sorts the work by Campaign, Copywriting, Digital, Identity and Positioning.

The site is a Webflow build. The sitemap lists 25 work pages. The footer reads 2024. It shows no prices.
pricing_detail: No published rates. Contact is by email to hello@thatthing.com or by phone.
agent_guidance:
Use That Thing as a reference for a brand studio that leads with writing as much as design. Each project has a one-line summary in plain text, so the homepage reads well as data.

The filter tags show the service mix: copywriting and positioning sit next to identity. Use the sitemap to reach the 25 work pages. Expect no prices.
why_it_matters: It shows a studio that sells verbal identity and positioning next to visual identity, with short project lines that carry the idea.
tier_reason: Twelve named projects with one-line summaries, a service filter and 25 work pages in the sitemap. Held below A because the homepage gives no scope or results, no prices, and no llms.txt.

name: Jordan Jenkins
tagline: Welsh creative director's brand practice, Jkane, with an app-like layout and English and Welsh copy
description:
Jkane is the creative practice of Jordan Jenkins, a Welsh designer. The bio says he has over 15 years of experience, including Principal and Director roles. The work covers branding, strategy, illustration and animation.

The site has three case studies: Vizcom, ChatPRD and Beans. A Playground grid holds logos, mascots, decks and posters for brands such as Lamar, Teller, Solana and Mighty Networks. A logo row names past clients, among them Google, Discord, Riot Games and Khan Academy.

The site is a Next.js build with its content in the page data. Most texts have a Welsh version next to the English one.
agent_guidance:
Use this as a reference for a designer portfolio laid out like a desktop app, with an info panel and a large Playground grid. The static HTML shows only the menu and a newsletter line. The bio, the case texts and the image captions are in the __NEXT_DATA__ JSON, so read that or use a browser.

The contact email in the page data reads conact@jkane.co, with a missing letter. Most text fields have a Welsh version.
why_it_matters: It is a brand designer portfolio with full English and Welsh copy, which is rare, and a large playground of logo and mascot work.
tier_reason: Three case studies with full texts, a large Playground grid and a bio with years of experience. Held below A because the static HTML is a shell, there are only three cases, and there is no sitemap or llms.txt.

name: FRA
tagline: Milan doodle designer Francesco Caporale, with 56 projects across illustration, murals and live painting
description:
FRA! is the portfolio of Francesco Caporale, a doodle designer and illustrator in Milan. The bio says he graduated in Graphic Design & Art Direction from NABA in 2014 and then started doodle art. The site is in Italian.

The homepage counts 56 projects and shows three: a Xiaomi Guinness World Record drawing, an IKEA live-painting campaign and a WAMI shop window. A client row names Vodafone, Walt Disney, Nespresso, Moleskine, Superga and Vans, among others. Services include advertising graphics, illustration, art direction, murals, live painting and workshops.

The site runs on WordPress with the Divi theme. It has a shop link and no prices on the homepage.
agent_guidance:
Use FRA as a reference for an illustrator portfolio where the drawing style runs through the whole interface. The homepage text is in Italian.

Some project text shows broken characters (for example in the Xiaomi blurb), and the footer reads "©20XX". Do not copy those.
why_it_matters: It shows how an illustrator with one signature style turns that style into the site itself, backed by a long client list.
tier_reason: 56 projects and a long list of named brand clients. Held at C because the homepage shows only three projects, some text has encoding errors, and there is no llms.txt.

name: Lax Chee
tagline: Creative director and developer portfolio built as a WebGL scene with keyboard controls
description:
Lax Space is the portfolio of Lax Chee, a digital creative director and front-end developer. The meta description names UI/UX, branding and front-end work in React and TypeScript.

The homepage is a WebGL scene with a small HUD: points, an FPS counter, Orbit on [Tab] and Rewind on [Space]. A works list names 12 projects, among them Stamped, Fukuda, Motion Blue, Sake of Nada, Utsubo and OEDO Food Hall, most tagged with roles such as Branding, Design and FE Dev. A link opens a sandbox.

The site is a Next.js build. The sitemap lists one URL per project.
agent_guidance:
Use this as a reference for a creative-developer portfolio where the hero is an interactive 3D scene with game-style controls. The scene is canvas only, so read it in a browser. The works list and role tags are in the HTML.

The page shows "Font-end Developer" with a missing letter. Pair this pattern with a real 3D stack such as three.js or react-three-fiber.
why_it_matters: It turns a project list into a playable 3D object, which proves the developer half of the role on the first screen.
tier_reason: A working WebGL hero with keyboard controls, and 12 named projects with role tags. Held below A because the case texts are not in the HTML, the page has a typo, and there is no llms.txt.
